Project.name: letopis
Project.annotation: A temporal, versioned entity store over PostgreSQL/TimescaleDB with a chainable graph-query API, a DB-driven schema registry, and built-in authentication, ACL, and sessions.
Project.keywords: temporal database, versioned entities, event history, graph traversal, chainable query, schema registry, acl, authentication, sessions, postgres, timescaledb, redis

Actors.actor-Developer: Library consumer building an application: models the domain, opens connections, and reads/writes/traverses entities through the chain API.
Actors.actor-Operator: Administers accounts, credentials, and ACL resources/rules, and manages the domain schema (seed / schema-sync).
Actors.actor-EndUser: An authenticated account whose credentials, sessions, and permissions letopis manages — interacts indirectly, through an app built on the library.
Actors.actor-System: Automated actor: dev bootstrap (up), codegen/schema tooling, and change-watch consumers.

UC-001.Action: Open a store connection with connect()/up()
UC-001.Goal: Obtain a working EntityDb bound to a schema + partition
UC-001.Preconditions: A reachable PostgreSQL with the schema applied (or Docker available for up())
UC-001.AcceptanceCriteria: connect() returns an EntityDb; enforceAcl without an account throws; unknown account throws

UC-002.Action: Define or synchronize the domain schema (Schema table)
UC-002.Goal: Have the class registry reflect the intended domain model safely
UC-002.Preconditions: A schema JSON (for sync) or a seed; DB access
UC-002.AcceptanceCriteria: loadRegistry resolves classes/ancestors/link ends; schema-sync reports diffs and blocks breaking changes without --apply

UC-003.Action: Create an entity of a class
UC-003.Goal: Persist a validated, versioned entity with a proper id
UC-003.Preconditions: Class exists and is non-abstract; an account is set
UC-003.AcceptanceCriteria: A new Entity version row exists; ValidationError on invalid data; v5 ids computed from declared ends/fields, else v7/v4

UC-004.Action: Read and traverse the graph (class + link ends / pivots)
UC-004.Preconditions: Registry loaded; links declared in Schema
UC-004.AcceptanceCriteria: Correct forward/reverse traversal; latest-version reads by default; unknown paths throw a clear error

UC-005.Goal: Apply a change while preserving full history
UC-005.AcceptanceCriteria: A new version is inserted (deep-merged patch); prior versions remain queryable

UC-006.Goal: Tombstone the target and its dependents consistently
UC-006.Preconditions: Authorized for DELETE; confirm for filterless deletes
UC-006.AcceptanceCriteria: Target + dependents tombstoned via the entity_delete trigger; "acl denies DELETE" when unauthorized

UC-007.Action: Run a temporal query (asOf, versions, history, after cursor)
UC-007.Goal: Reconstruct point-in-time state and paginate history deterministically
UC-007.AcceptanceCriteria: asOf(t) returns the state as of t; versions() lists history; after(cursor) does stable keyset pagination

UC-008.Action: Authenticate via password / API key / key+secret / TOTP / OTP / identity link
UC-008.Goal: Prove identity without leaking secrets or timing
UC-008.Preconditions: A credential exists for the identity
UC-008.AcceptanceCriteria: AuthResult on success, null on failure; constant-time compares; dummy-verify on unknown identifier; invalid base32 TOTP secret throws

UC-009.Goal: Track authenticated sessions with TTL over Redis
UC-009.AcceptanceCriteria: Token stored hashed (sha256) with TTL; check returns Session or null; revokeAll clears an account's sessions

UC-010.Action: Enforce ACL on reads and writes
UC-010.Goal: Restrict access per account by Resource/Rule with weighted precedence
UC-010.AcceptanceCriteria: Deny-by-default; highest-weight matching rule wins; row filters injected into reads; denied writes throw

UC-011.Goal: React to inserts/versions/tombstones in near real time
UC-011.AcceptanceCriteria: WatchEvent delivered on change; reconnect invokes onReconnect

UC-012.Goal: Queue several plans and execute them efficiently in one round
UC-012.AcceptanceCriteria: Pure-insert plans fast-pathed into one multi-insert; results returned per queued plan; discard() clears the queue

UC-013.Action: Bootstrap a dev environment with up()
UC-013.Goal: Get a ready Postgres+Redis with schema and seeds applied
UC-013.Preconditions: Docker installed (unless dsn points at a running Postgres)
UC-013.AcceptanceCriteria: Container provisioned, schema+seeds applied, readiness awaited, connected; actionable errors on docker missing / timeout / bad schema|version

UC-014.Action: Generate types / synchronize schema via the CLIs
UC-014.Goal: Keep TypeScript types and the DB schema aligned safely
UC-014.Preconditions: DSN + schema; a schema JSON for sync
UC-014.AcceptanceCriteria: gen-types emits a typed .d.ts facade; schema-sync applies only non-breaking changes (or with explicit --apply)

NonGoals.item-1: Not a code-first ORM: class definitions live in the DB Schema table, not as TS classes; there are no code migrations.
NonGoals.item-2: No arbitrary-SQL query builder beyond the chain DSL and the fixed auth/authz table APIs.
NonGoals.item-3: No admin UI for ACL — authorization is rule/weight based and configured as data.
NonGoals.item-4: Dev Redis sessions are ephemeral (no persistence/password in the dev container).

Constraints.constraint-1: Requires PostgreSQL 17 with the TimescaleDB extension (Entity is a hypertable); Redis for sessions.
Constraints.constraint-2: ESM-only; Node 20+ with NodeNext resolution and explicit .js import specifiers.
Constraints.constraint-3: Entity.account is NOT NULL — every write needs an account (connect({account}) or the seeded System account).
Constraints.constraint-4: up() requires Docker unless the dsn targets an already-running Postgres.

Risks.risk-1: Invariant duplication: entity validation and link-end rules live both in M-DDL triggers and in M-WRITE.validate — they can drift.
Risks.risk-2: ACL (M-ACL) concentrates authorization logic and is compiled into a memoized per-connection enforcer, so a wrong rule/weight silently widens access; covered by lib/test/acl.test.ts plus enforcement paths in lib/test/salon.test.ts.
Risks.risk-3: Type-level import cycle M-SQL↔M-ACL↔M-TABLES and runtime ESM cycle M-CONNECT↔M-UP constrain refactoring.
Risks.risk-4: Logic concentration in chain.ts / sql.ts / write.ts — most of the engine lives in three files, raising regression surface.
Risks.risk-5: The demo booking schema is seeded by hand (lib/sql/seed.booking.sql) and is the source of truth for its classes, so a hand edit can silently diverge from the docs; the class count in the file header is checked by lib/scripts/check-docs.mjs.

answer-1.was: Are gen-types/schema-sync supported product surface or internal tooling?

ResolvedQuestions.answer-1: Supported product surface. Both ship in the npm tarball (package.json "files" includes "scripts", added in 0.18.1), are documented in README §10.9/§10.11 and §11, are self-contained plain Node (no tsx needed), and gen-types output is guarded by a drift test in lib/test/wave2.test.ts that compiles the generated .d.ts. They are not installed as bin — invoke with node node_modules/letopis/scripts/<name>.mjs.

answer-2.was: Is the demo booking domain part of the shipped product or a fixture?

ResolvedQuestions.answer-2: Shipped, as the default fixture. seed.booking.sql is inside "files" (sql/) and up() applies it when the seeds option is omitted, so a consumer who forgets seeds gets the booking classes in their own schema — called out as a warning in README §1.1. It is the source of truth for its own classes, hand-edited, and its class count is asserted by lib/scripts/check-docs.mjs.

OpenQuestions.question-1: What is the intended security posture for enforceAcl/enforceAccount in production? Both default to false today (opt-in), i.e. an app that forgets them gets no tenant isolation and no authorization on reads; deciding whether that default should invert is an owner policy call, not a fact derivable from the code.
